title: God of Eternal Love
description: God of Eternal Love in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 106, part 2, headed “Israel punished and pardoned; or, God's unchangeable love”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God of e-ter-nal love, How fick-le are our ways! And yet how oft did Is-rael prove Thy con-stan-cy of grace!

lines: And yet how oft did Israel prove
And then thy praise they sung;
But soon thy works of power forgot,
Now with their lusts provoke the Lord,
Yet when they mourn'd their faults,
Brought his own covenant to his thoughts,
And call'd them still his sons.
Their names were in his book,
He sav'd them from their foes;
Oft he chastis'd, but ne'er forsook
And Christians join the solemn word

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
